chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام would say in his prostration:

O Allah, if I have disobeyed You, then I have obeyed You in the most beloved of things to You, and that is faith in You, as a favor from You upon me, not as a favor from me upon You. And I have abandoned disobeying You in the most hateful of things to You, and that is that I should ascribe to You a child or ascribe to You a partner, as a favor from You upon me, not as a favor from me upon You. And I have disobeyed You in matters not by way of defiance, nor stubborn opposition, nor out of arrogance against Your worship, nor denial of Your Lordship; rather, I followed my desire, and Satan caused me to slip after the proof against me and the clarification. So if You punish me, then it is for my sins, without being unjust to me; and if You forgive me and have mercy on me, then it is by Your munificence and by Your generosity, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: faith in Allah as the most beloved act of obedience mentioned in the supplication
key_terms.الْبَيَانِ: the clarification and clear explanation that had already come
key_terms.الْحُجَّةِ: the proof established against the servant before his lapse
key_terms.بِجُودِكَ: by Your munificence, indicating that forgiveness comes through divine generosity
key_terms.بِذُنُوبِي: because of my sins, acknowledging personal responsibility for punishment
key_terms.رُبُوبِيَّتِكَ: Your Lordship, whose denial the supplicant explicitly negates
key_terms.شَرِيكًا: a partner ascribed to Allah, referring to shirk which the supplication rejects
key_terms.مَعْصِيَتَكَ: disobedience against Allah, acknowledged and contrasted with obedience

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام say in sujud while asking Allah for forgiveness and mercy?
ai.summary: This supplication of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام combines confession of sin with affirmation of tawhid and iman. It acknowledges that faith and avoidance of shirk are divine favors, while seeking forgiveness through Allah’s justice, generosity, and mercy.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.977 - Imam Ali ibn al-Hussain (as) would say in his prostration:
Allahumma in kuntu qad ‘asaytuka fa-inni qad ata‘tuka fi ahabbi al-ashya’i ilayka wa huwa al-imanu bika, manna minka ‘alayya la manna minni ‘alayka. Wa taraktu ma‘siyataka fi abghadi al-ashya’i ilayka wa huwa an ad‘uwa laka waladan aw ad‘uwa laka shareekan, manna minka ‘alayya la manna minni ‘alayka. Wa ‘asaytuka fi ashya’a ‘ala ghayri wajhi mukabarah wa la mu‘anadah wa la istikbaran ‘an ‘ibadatik wa la juhudan lirububiyyatik, walakin ittaba‘tu hawaya wa istazallani ash-shaytan ba‘da al-hujjati ‘alayya wa al-bayan.

Fa-in tu‘adhdhibni fabi-dhunoobi ghayra zalimin li, wa in taghfir li wa tarhamni fabi-joodika wa bi-karamika, ya arham ar-raahimeen
“O’ Allah (swt), if I have disobeyed You, then I have also obeyed You in the most beloved of things to You, which is faith in You, a favour from You to me, not a favour from me to You. I have refrained from disobeying You in the most detestable things to You, which is to claim a child for You or to call upon a partner for You, a favour from You to me, not a favour from me to You. I have sinned against You in certain things, but not out of defiance, enmity, arrogance in worship, or denial of Your Lord (azj)ship. Rather, I followed my desires and the devil led me astray after the evidence and guidance were made clear to me. If You punish me, it is for my sins, without injustice to me. And if You forgive and have mercy on me, it is due to Your generosity and kindness, O’ Most Merciful of the merciful.”
